input.head: fix/settings-session-preferences
input.title: fix: separate preferred FPS from live efficiency settings
input.body:
## Summary

```text
preferred FPS ───────────────→ saved profile / pause highlight
live FPS ← efficiency90/50   → stage clock
menu instance selector      →65/50 on efficiency changes
```

Recover settings state and persistence before the native screen rewrite. Existing controls now update both rates correctly; efficiency retains the preference and remains session-only.

## Evidence

- **Before:** FPS and efficiency state are conflated and every setting saves immediately.
  **After:** normal menu changes save when Settings closes; efficiency saves immediately with preferred FPS. Reload retains low quality/audio-off choices while restoring preferred FPS and clearing efficiency.
- Source audit corrected a backlog error: pause highlights preferred35 at live90 or50 (PauseMenu914–943/pcode5492–5603). Menu retains its separate65/50 selector across Settings reopen, resetting on a new menu instance.
- Re-clicking selected controls still performs the source action. Both native/mock cases verify mouse and keyboard radio activation, preference saving, reload and retained selector lifetimes.
- Formatting, TypeScript,450 tests /5750 assertions and build pass. All15 affected native/mock browser cases pass; four session cases pass after removing a nonfunctional wrapper, followed by both repeat-action cases with keyboard assertions.
- Native screen rendering, complete event/save ordering and original pixel/game parity remain open. Legacy90-only saves use a documented50FPS fallback because their old preference is unrecoverable. Requested zoom still saves immediately.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** settings

Changes preferred-rate serialization, efficiency reset behavior, save timing and existing control callbacks. Preserves the key-input correction and dialog focus handling from #30. No original media is committed.

## Summary

```text
browser code → logical key → profile / GameInput / Dialog
input frame → duplicate-axis priority + Space latch + lock edge
```

Recover the input portion of the settings backlog before the screen rewrite. Modifier/Enter aliases share logical codes, supported bindings survive profile validation, and either alias can resume through the pause dialog.

## Evidence

- **Before:** duplicate axis bindings activate both directions; Space fires even when horizontally bound; the backlog lock callback fires twice for two physical aliases.
  **After:** real keyboard proofs retain Up/Left priority, cross-axis sharing, source Space latches and one frame-sampled lock edge. A press/release between frames does not trigger lock.
- Ran the alias regression against backlog input: red with locks2 versus1. Restored the corrected controller; all12 affected native/mock browser cases pass, including actual-game modifier pause/resume, player clocks, focus and audio. The new test waits for canvas readiness; no sleep/assertion removal.
- Formatting, TypeScript,445 tests /5725 assertions and production build pass. Source/pcode audit confirms labels (including F1 → lowercase p), duplicate binding semantics and the frame latch.
- Preserves the same-commit Dialog focus repair. FPS/session and the full settings picker remain separate work; browser code/layout translation, the bounded whitelist and original insertion-order movement remain explicit limits. Full-game parity is unproven.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** controls

Changes profile key validation, gameplay key handling and dialog shortcuts. The development fixture uses the production validator/controller; no original media is committed.

output.body:
## Summary

```text
preferred FPS ───────────────→ saved profile / pause highlight
live FPS ← efficiency90/50   → stage clock
menu instance selector      →65/50 on efficiency changes
```

Recover settings state and persistence before the native screen rewrite. Existing controls now update both rates correctly; efficiency retains the preference and remains session-only.

## Evidence

- **Before:** FPS and efficiency state are conflated and every setting saves immediately.
  **After:** normal menu changes save when Settings closes; efficiency saves immediately with preferred FPS. Reload retains low quality/audio-off choices while restoring preferred FPS and clearing efficiency.
- Source audit corrected a backlog error: pause highlights preferred35 at live90 or50 (PauseMenu914–943/pcode5492–5603). Menu retains its separate65/50 selector across Settings reopen, resetting on a new menu instance.
- Re-clicking selected controls still performs the source action. Both native/mock cases verify mouse and keyboard radio activation, preference saving, reload and retained selector lifetimes.
- Formatting, TypeScript,450 tests /5750 assertions and build pass. All15 affected native/mock browser cases pass; four session cases pass after removing a nonfunctional wrapper, followed by both repeat-action cases with keyboard assertions.
- Native screen rendering, complete event/save ordering and original pixel/game parity remain open. Legacy90-only saves use a documented50FPS fallback because their old preference is unrecoverable. Requested zoom still saves immediately.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** settings

Changes preferred-rate serialization, efficiency reset behavior, save timing and existing control callbacks. Preserves the key-input correction and dialog focus handling from #30. No original media is committed.
